clue.text: Male teachers are ahead, say, providing spice

indicators.note: the teachers' letters are placed in front of the male's letter

parts.note: the NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union
say signals an example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A staffroom of mostly male teachers somehow leading the way while handing round the seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are ahead' tells you the teachers' union (NUT, Britain's National Union of Teachers) comes before M.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of a tropical tree is grated as a common culinary spice.

clue.text: Extremely strange inside an operating system, and not just for men

indicators.note: inside places the outer letters within the operating system

parts.note: Unix is a well-known computer operating system

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of strange

explanation.surface: Something very odd inside a computer system, open to women as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' picks the two end letters of 'strange'. Unix is a computer operating system.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing or facilities suitable for both sexes are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Cutting miles, perhaps, dance round city complex

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the dance and ring go inside
perhaps signals the letters of miles are one possible arrangement

parts.note: the galop is a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dance that shortens the distance around a confusing city layout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of 'miles'; 'Cutting' has the dance plus O slice into that rearrangement after its first two letters. The galop is a quick 19th-century dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban sprawl formed by several merging cities is a very large conurbation of this kind.

clue.text: First to use old coin made of gold and iron?

parts.note: the guinea was an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings
pig is crude cast iron, as in pig iron

explanation.surface: Asking which came first: a gold coin or an iron one.
explanation.walkthrough: The guinea was a gold coin worth 21 shillings, used in Britain until 1814.
explanation.definitionFit: A test subject is the first person on whom something new is tried.

clue.text: One doesn't stop exam success, hesitation aside

parts.note: to pass is to succeed in an exam
er is the sound of someone hesitating
by can mean to one side, as in 'put by' or 'stand by'

explanation.surface: A student who keeps going regardless, getting through the exam despite some umming and erring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone walking past keeps moving rather than stopping, a playful paraphrase of the passer's role.

clue.text: Verbally subjected to coercion over northern city

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the synonym is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: pressed means forced or coerced
on can mean over, as in 'on top of'

explanation.surface: A city spoken of as having been bullied.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Lancashire in north-west England, famous for its football club North End.

clue.text: Prescribed books used up for scrap

parts.note: set books are those prescribed for study

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Required reading is worn out and thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used up' turns OT (Old Testament) to TO in a down clue. 'scrap' looks like rubbish but is a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a brief fight or quarrel, and so is a set-to.

clue.text: Centre of storm? Yes, it sounds like it

indicators.note: sounds like says the synonym is heard, not written

parts.note: aye is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Asking whether the heart of a storm is what it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The calm middle of a hurricane is named after the organ of sight.

clue.text: Worthless horse I caught beginning to eat chaff

indicators.note: caught means holding something, so the letter is held between the parts

parts.note: bad means of poor quality, worthless
a nag is an old horse

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of eat

explanation.surface: A poor horse I caught starts eating its feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaff' looks like horse feed but means teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff as a noun is playful teasing banter, the same as witty repartee.

clue.text: Very large college, variable in its education at first

parts.note: King's is a college at both Cambridge and London

indicators.note: in places the variable inside the two initial letters
at first takes the opening letters of the words its and education

parts.note: Z is a typical algebraic variable letter

explanation.surface: A huge college whose teaching puts variables first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives I and E from 'its education'; 'in' puts Z inside them, making IZE after KINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: King-size describes products of extra large dimensions, such as beds or cigarettes.

clue.text: Initially too puny to be like country gentry

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the following word too

parts.note: weedy means thin and feeble, so puny

explanation.surface: Someone too slight to pass as a member of the landed set.
explanation.definitionFit: Country squires stereotypically wear tweed jackets, so tweedy describes their style.

clue.text: Sound chap at edge of revolutionary circle?

indicators.note: sound tells us the following synonym is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a chap is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: A sensible man on the fringe of a radical political group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests politics but means turning: the circle is a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The rim of a spoked wheel, the outer edge of a turning circle, is called by this name.

clue.text: Player who may be employed on a sliding scale

definitions.text: Player who may be employed on a sliding scale

parts.words: Player who may be employed on a sliding scale
parts.note: a sliding scale sounds like pay rates, but here it is a musical scale played by moving a slide

explanation.surface: A worker paid according to a flexible wage system.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument changes pitch with a sliding tube, so its scales literally slide.

clue.text: Offering protection from missile — like a shot!

definitions.text: Offering protection from missile — like a shot!

parts.words: Offering protection from missile — like a shot!
parts.note: shielding from a projectile, with 'like a shot' playing on the shot being the very thing kept out

explanation.surface: Quick protection from something thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Vests or glass able to stop a fired round are described this way.

clue.text: Close song out, when music starts to die

indicators.note: starts means the music comes at the beginning

parts.note: pop is a genre of music

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer finishing a number as the music begins to fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CLOSE SONG into ONES CLOGS; 'starts' puts POP in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang idiom meaning to pass away, from clog shoes being given up.

clue.text: Draw attention to illegal drug in flimsy container

indicators.note: in places the drug inside the flimsy word

parts.note: slight means flimsy, acting as the container here
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Smugglers hide drugs in a cheap flimsy box to draw attention away.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight something is to focus the public gaze on it, like a stage lamp.

clue.text: Comprehensive school's head showing signs of distress

indicators.note: head takes the first letter of school's

parts.note: weeping is crying, a sign of distress

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school headteacher in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' looks like part of 'school' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide-ranging, all-embracing changes are described as complete or far-reaching.

clue.text: Derelict area half dark, but with fresh air, nonetheless

parts.note: dusk, neither light nor fully dark, is twilight

indicators.note: read as 'none the less': O, looking like zero or none, is dropped

parts.note: ozone is jokingly used for bracing seaside air

explanation.surface: A rundown district that is gloomy yet somehow breezy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' is read as none (O) less, taking an O from OZONE to leave ZONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Planners use the term for a decaying urban district between centre and suburbs.

clue.text: Shoot a number of rooks initially, wearing turned-up hat

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: wearing means the hat goes round the letter
turned-up in a down clue means the hat is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of rooks

explanation.surface: Firing at rooks while wearing a hat with its brim turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned-up' reverses LID to DIL; R sits inside it, giving DRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's slender climbing shoot that coils round supports is called this.

clue.text: African very maligned? Not half

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'

indicators.note: not half means only half of maligned survives, its first four letters

explanation.surface: Is an African very badly spoken of? Hardly at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much', adding to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Somalia in the Horn of Africa is so named.

clue.text: National scandal ultimately Newham's undoing

indicators.note: undoing suggests taking apart and rebuilding the letters
ultimately takes the last letter of the word scandal

explanation.surface: A national scandal that finally ruins the London borough of Newham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives L, which joins NEWHAMS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A national here is a citizen of a country; one from Wales fits.

clue.text: Combine to throw gang leader in lake

indicators.note: throw in means the leader is put inside the lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of gang

explanation.surface: Uniting to drown a gang boss in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Merge means to join together or amalgamate.

clue.text: Paid nothing to feed prisoner's, best friend?

indicators.note: to feed means to go into, so these letters go inside the prisoner

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag
pd is the abbreviation for paid
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An inmate's closest pal gets nothing for his trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to feed' puts the payment and the zero inside the convict; 'old lag' is British slang for a long-serving prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog is called man's best friend, and a pampered small pet is a classic example.

clue.text: Town crier's double, one helping to deliver changes?

definitions.meaning: a town crier rings a handbell to call attention
a bell-... sounds changes, the sequences of change ringing

explanation.surface: The town crier's lookalike assists in bringing about reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' sounds political but refers to change ringing on church bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: the bell-swinging crier, a lookalike, and a member of a bell-ringing team.

clue.text: It may be natural to chew the fat

definitions.meaning: natural fuel from underground deposits is this
to chat idly, which is to ... in informal speech

explanation.definitionFit: Natural gas is a fuel, and to gas is informal for chattering at length.

clue.text: Local serving beer no one inside rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole is read backwards
inside places no and one within the beer

parts.note: lager is a type of beer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pub serving beer, yet nobody inside will drink it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns round the whole beer-with-insert, giving LANOIGER backwards. 'Local' looks like the pub but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Local and regional both describe something belonging to a particular district.

clue.text: Urges fellow Liberals to see China

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
he stands for a male, a fellow
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Pressing a fellow party member to visit China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is the porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell china is a very thin, delicate kind of porcelain.

clue.text: Argument during Indian lunch

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: A row breaking out over a meal in India.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Indian usage this word names a light midday meal or a packed lunch.
